title: Telemetry: time-to-ready metrics (overall + per-stage) and provisioning error categorization w/ cardinality safeguards
author: Logan Wright
release_notes:
- Adds provisioning time-to-ready telemetry (overall + per-stage histograms)
- Adds standardized error categorization for provisioning stages
- Implements cardinality safeguards (tag allowlists, normalization, truncation, and sampling for high-volume events)
description:
Context: Part of the Provision-to-ready automation sprint. We need a single source of truth for “time-to-ready” across the provisioning pipeline with stage breakdowns, plus error categorization that is stable enough to alert on and dashboard against without blowing up metric cardinality.

What this PR does: 1) Adds “time-to-ready” metrics as histograms for overall duration (Requested → Ready) and per-stage durations (Requested→Provisioning, Provisioning→Imaging, Imaging→Bootstrapping, Bootstrapping→Validating, Validating→Ready). 2) Introduces a canonical provisioning error taxonomy (category + reason) used across stage failures, and plumbs it into structured events + metrics. 3) Adds explicit cardinality safeguards to avoid unbounded label growth from pool_id/customer_id/region variations and raw error strings.

Metrics added/updated: - redwood.provisioning.time_to_ready_seconds (histogram): overall duration, with tags: environment, region, sku, pool_tier, result. - redwood.provisioning.stage_duration_seconds (histogram): per-stage duration, with tags: environment, region, sku, pool_tier, stage, result. - redwood.provisioning.stage_failures_total (counter): failures, with tags: environment, region, sku, pool_tier, stage, error_category, error_reason. - redwood.provisioning.runs_total (counter): run starts/completions, tags: environment, region, sku, pool_tier, result.

Tagging and cardinality policy (enforced in code): - No pool_id, customer_id, cluster_name, request_id, or correlation_id tags on metrics. Those remain in structured logs/events only. - region and sku are normalized to a known allowlist; unknown values collapse to "unknown" and emit a single structured warning event (rate-limited) so we can update allowlists if needed. - error_reason is limited to a controlled enum (see ProvisioningErrorReason). Raw provider errors are captured in structured events as error_detail (truncated), not as metric labels. - All string tag values are lowercased and truncated to 64 chars; invalid UTF-8 replaced.

Error taxonomy: - error_category: infra | imaging | bootstrap | validation | control_plane | quota | config | network | security | unknown - error_reason: enum of stable “why” codes (e.g., iam_denied, quota_exceeded, terraform_apply_failed, image_pull_timeout, helm_values_invalid, dns_resolution_failed, tls_handshake_failed, gpu_ecc_error, perf_canary_failed, state_conflict, timeout).

Implementation notes: - Uses a single helper (ProvisioningTelemetry.emitStageTransition) to record duration, counters, and event payload consistently. - Histograms use fixed bucket strategy (seconds): [30, 60, 120, 300, 600, 1200, 2400, 3600, 7200, 14400] to cover both “happy path” and degraded scenarios. - Adds a small “stage timing accumulator” on the run record so durations are derived from persisted timestamps rather than in-process timers (works across retries/restarts).

Rollout/compatibility: - Metrics names are new (no renames). - Existing structured provisioning events are extended with error_category/reason fields; consumers that ignore unknown fields are unaffected.

Screenshots/verification: - In staging, validated histograms populate for a simulated run with forced stage retries; confirmed no high-cardinality explosions (top 20 tag values remain bounded). - Backfill (ENG-2756) will use the same taxonomy mapping; this PR includes mapping helpers used by the backfill job.

Testing: - Unit tests for error mapping + tag normalization + allowlist behavior. - Integration test for stage duration emission on transition replay (persisted timestamps). - Manual: ran a staging provisioning run w/ induced DNS failure and confirmed stage_failures_total increments with error_category=network, error_reason=dns_resolution_failed.

Refs: ENG-2748, ENG-2749, ENG-2756. Related: PR-48232 (structured events + correlation IDs), PR-48241 (retry/backoff policy).
commits: telemetry: add time_to_ready and stage_duration histograms
metrics: enforce label allowlists + normalization + truncation
events: include error_category/reason on stage failure events
tests: add unit + integration coverage for telemetry helpers
snippet:
Example metric emission (simplified):

telemetry.ObserveHistogram(
  "redwood.provisioning.stage_duration_seconds",
  duration.Seconds(),
  Tags{
    "environment": env,
    "region": NormalizeRegion(region),
    "sku": NormalizeSKU(sku),
    "pool_tier": tier,
    "stage": string(stage),
    "result": resultTag,
  },
)

On failure:
telemetry.IncCounter(
  "redwood.provisioning.stage_failures_total",
  Tags{
    "environment": env,
    "region": NormalizeRegion(region),
    "sku": NormalizeSKU(sku),
    "pool_tier": tier,
    "stage": string(stage),
    "error_category": string(cat),
    "error_reason": string(reason),
  },
)

Cardinality guardrail: pool_id and correlation_id are intentionally excluded from all metric tags and only included in structured events as fields.

review_conversation: Aisha Bello: Can we confirm we’re not tagging pool_id/customer_id anywhere? Dashboards can join on events for drilldown, but metrics need to stay stable.
Logan Wright (author): Confirmed. I added an explicit denylist in tags.go (pool_id, customer_id, cluster_name, correlation_id, request_id). Tests assert those keys are rejected.

Caleb Johnson: Buckets look reasonable but stage durations can exceed 4h during quota/blocked situations. Are we OK with that saturating the last bucket? Also: please ensure the structured event includes raw duration_ms so traces can use it even if histogram saturates.

Logan Wright (author): Updated buckets to include 14400s (4h) and added duration_ms in the event payload. Beyond that will still fall into +Inf which is fine for alerts (we’ll page on “stuck stage” via separate logic).
Allison Grant: error_reason must be an enum; do not include provider error messages. Please double-check the mapping doesn’t accidentally embed terraform stderr as a reason.

Logan Wright (author): Fixed mapping.go to route terraform stderr into event.error_detail (truncated) and map reasons to terraform_apply_failed / terraform_plan_failed / terraform_state_lock_timeout only. Added unit test to ensure no whitespace/long strings make it into error_reason.
Rafael Mendes: For cardinality: region and sku allowlists will need updating. What happens for a new region we bring up? I’d rather not drop data silently.

Logan Wright (author): Unknown values map to "unknown" and emit a rate-limited structured warning event: provisioning.telemetry_unknown_tag_value with original value + tag name. That should keep metrics stable but still make it visible we need to update allowlists.
Ethan Park: The stage timing accumulator derived from persisted timestamps is the right approach. One ask: ensure transitions replay doesn’t double-observe when we re-process old events.
Logan Wright (author): Added a guard: only observe duration when a transition is first committed (run_record marks stage_observed=true per stage+attempt). Integration test covers replay path.
Aisha Bello: LGTM after the denylist test. Approved.
Allison Grant: Approved. Thanks for being strict about labels.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Logan Wright. Squash commit: 8f2c4d7f0c1f ("Telemetry: time-to-ready histograms + provisioning error taxonomy").
